Summit aids Mainland firms
body:
The 11th Belt & Road Summit entered its second day at the Convention & Exhibition Centre, featuring a newly introduced “Go Global Chapter” and a dedicated GoGlobal Connect Zone designed to assist Mainland enterprises in expanding their international footprint. 

 

Speaking at a thematic breakout session today, Secretary for Commerce & Economic Development Algernon Yau highlighted Hong Kong's role as the ideal platform for Mainland businesses venturing overseas. He noted that the Government’s GoGlobal Task Force has achieved substantial progress since its establishment last October.

 

“We have assisted over 300 Chinese Mainland enterprises in setting up or expanding business in Hong Kong; organised more than 20 promotional events; and engaged over 5,000 representatives of Chinese Mainland enterprises,” Mr Yau said.

 

He added that the Northern Metropolis development will unlock new land and prospects for Mainland companies to explore global opportunities. 

 

Business leaders attending the forum echoed these sentiments, pointing to Hong Kong's unique strategic advantages. Based at the Science and Technology Park since 2023, 3D mapping technology firm Chief Executive Officer Chen Li shared that operating in the city has accelerated her company's internationalisation by offering crucial expertise to navigate global market standards, including Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) frameworks.

 

Recalling her participation in a Chief Executive-led delegation to Central Asia in June, Ms Chen emphasised Hong Kong's influence, credibility and ability to build direct bridges with international stakeholders.

 

Similarly, Ren Junfei, founder and Chief Executive Officer of a financial services company, hailed the summit as an invaluable platform for gaining market insights across Belt & Road economies, noting that direct exchanges with consulates, embassies, government agencies and businesses pave a pathway for collaboration and opportunities.

title: Belt-Road Summit unlocks growth
body:
The 11th Belt & Road Summit opened today, bringing together over 6,000 participants, including over 100 government and business speakers, as well as over 100 delegations. More than 60 memoranda of understanding (MOUs) will be witnessed during the Summit.

 

Under the theme "Advancing High-quality Development • Embarking on a New Journey", the Summit aims to foster high-quality, sustainable and innovative development.

 

Speaking at the opening session, Chief Executive John Lee said, in addition to strengthening the city's relations with traditional partners, Hong Kong continues to expand its network of friends along the Belt and Road.

 

"I have led high-level business delegations to explore opportunities in 13 Belt and Road countries across the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), the Middle East and Central Asia, focusing on specific areas to explore new markets," Mr Lee said.

 

"These missions delivered over 250 MOUs and other agreements, from policy co-ordination and trade and investment, to expanded connectivity and support for companies. They underline Hong Kong's long-standing focus on opening new markets, forming new partnerships and advancing regional co-operation."

 

Mr Lee said these achievements demonstrate the value of a hub-to-hub co-operation model, where Hong Kong can serve as Belt and Road economies' gateway to the Chinese Mainland and global markets and the economies can connect Hong Kong with relevant regions. This interconnected network of hubs will amplify regional strengths through enhanced connectivity and unleash fresh opportunities.

 

Financial Secretary Paul Chan said ASEAN has consistently outpaced the global economy and is becoming an increasingly important partner in technological advancement and industrial upgrading. Two-way trade between China and ASEAN surpassed US$1 trillion last year, reflecting the reshaping of industrial chains across the region.

 

He stated that ASEAN's demographic, market and technology dividends offer growth opportunities through its young population, expanding middle class, trade agreements and AI. Turning these advantages into sustained growth requires patient capital, open, well-regulated testing grounds and a strong talent base. Hong Kong can connect global investors with innovative companies, drawing on the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area's frontier research, advanced manufacturing and substantial consumer market. The Northern Metropolis will facilitate the flow of technology, talent and capital, strengthening connections between research, commercial application and production to foster shared prosperity across the region.

 

Secretary for Justice Paul Lam noted that the arbitration ecosystem in Hong Kong is equally world-renowned, the city is the second most preferred arbitral seat in the world, and the most preferred arbitral seat in Asia Pacific. Together with the headquarters of the International Organization for Mediation established in Hong Kong, which is dedicated to resolving international disputes through mediation, all these reinforce the city's status as an international legal and dispute resolution services centre.

 

Secretary for Commerce & Economic Development Algernon Yau highlighted that Hong Kong is steadfast in promoting trade for the benefit of all, through upholding a rules-based multilateral trading system, implementing transparent and non-discriminatory regulations, and facilitating customs and digital interoperability.

 

The Summit witnessed seven MOUs between the HKSAR Government and their overseas counterparts to promote bilateral co-operation and exchanges, covering the Commerce and Economic Development Bureau, the Working Group on Developing Low-altitude Economy, the Independent Commission Against Corruption, the Belt and Road Office, Invest Hong Kong and the Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau, with Bangladesh, Kazakhstan, Morocco, Thailand, Turkey, Zimbabwe, and Uzbekistan.

 

The Summit also witnessed around 55 other MOUs in various areas. The total value of these MOUs, together with new projects and deals finalised before and during the Summit, is over US$3.1 billion.

title: Youth explore aerospace science
body:
Hong Kong and Macau youth joined a "Tiangong Class" today to engage with space experts and the Shenzhou-23 crew currently carrying out a manned space mission on the Chinese Space Station.

 

Mission commander Zhu Yangzhu, astronaut Zhang Zhiyuan and Hong Kong's first payload expert Lai Ka-ying served as "space teachers" to deliver expert lectures to students, conduct real-time science experiments, and engage in an interactive "dialogue between space and Earth".

 

Organised by the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government, the Macao SAR Government, and the China Manned Space Agency, the "Tiangong Class" Hong Kong and Macao Designated Session was held at Ms Lai's alma mater, Tsuen Wan Public Ho Chuen Yiu Memorial College.

 

Over 200 participants attended the session, which featured in-orbit demonstrations, expert lectures and a question-and-answer session. The participants included primary and secondary school teachers and pupils from Hong Kong and Macao, alongside tertiary students, researchers, technology professionals, and youth organisation representatives.

 

The session lasted approximately 1.5 hours, during which Ms Lai introduced the operational process of the Multi-Spectral Imaging Carbon Observatory (MUSICO). Developed by the Hong Kong University of Science & Technology, MUSICO undertakes the important task of monitoring global greenhouse gases, contributing to national aerospace programmes and global sustainable development.

 

The astronauts also introduced the Tiangong Space Station’s facilities, including the core module instruments and experimental facilities, the space vegetable garden, the space kitchen and space food, and shared their daily lives and scientific research work on the space station.

 

Speaking at the event, Chief Executive John Lee thanked the China Manned Space Agency for its support, as well as the various organisations and departments for their joint efforts, which have enabled students from Hong Kong and Macao to learn from the astronauts aboard the Tiangong Space Station.

 

Mr Lee noted that, over the more than 30 years of the development of China's manned space programme, every step has embodied the Chinese nation's indomitable spirit of self-improvement and courage in exploration.

 

He added that when the delegation from China's manned space programme visited Hong Kong in 2023, it sowed three important seeds for the city: a seed to foster national pride, a seed to explore science and technology, and a seed to encourage the pursuit of dreams. As Hong Kong's aerospace research and development has progressed from ground-based support to in-orbit operations in space, enabling Hong Kong people to explore the cosmos, it demonstrates that these seeds have not only taken root and sprouted, but are also thriving.

 

Mr Lee also encouraged all sectors of society, particularly young people, to actively participate in the science popularisation and awareness-raising activities currently organised by the Hong Kong SAR Government under the theme "A Shared Cosmic Vision for National Rejuvenation".

 

He expressed the hope that the younger generation would look to astronauts as role models, serving the nation in building a strong aerospace country, thereby writing a brilliant chapter for the Chinese nation.

title: CE meets foreign officials in HK
body:
Chief Executive John Lee today met with senior government officials from Uzbekistan, Uruguay, Laos, Kazakhstan and Qatar who were in Hong Kong for the 11th Belt & Road Summit, welcoming their delegations and exchanging views on issues of mutual concern.

 

Mr Lee met with the Prime Minister of Uzbekistan Abdulla Nigmatovich Aripov at Government House. He noted that both sides, building on government-to-government high-level contacts and established ties, have pressed ahead with the results achieved during his earlier visit to Uzbekistan, and are closely following up on co-operation in legal services, trade, investment, education, innovation and technology, transport and logistics, culture, and talent development. Both sides will also continue discussions on bilateral agreements in various areas.

 

Mr Lee also noted that Uzbekistan is an important trading partner for Hong Kong in Central Asia. Hong Kong can provide strong support to Uzbekistan in trade and professional services. Both sides will continue to work together to promote co-operation in various areas, further consolidate their advantages as gateways for trade and investment, respectively in the Asia-Pacific and Central Asian regions, and jointly participate in the high-quality development of the Belt & Road Initiative to seize opportunities together and achieve mutual benefits.

 

The Chief Executive then met the Vice President of Uruguay Carolina Cosse. He said Hong Kong will continue to serve as a functional platform for the Belt & Road Initiative, leveraging the dual advantage of enjoying both national and global opportunities, to assist enterprises from the Global South in exploring the Asian market and seizing the immense opportunities of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area.

 

Mr Lee added that there is immense potential for co-operation between Hong Kong and Uruguay, and expressed the hope that both sides will strengthen collaboration in trade and investment, finance and professional services, and share the fruits of development together.

 

Mr Lee also met the Deputy Prime Minister of Laos Saleumxay Kommasith. He said the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government has established a Hong Kong Economic & Trade Office in Kuala Lumpur to deepen economic and trade co-operation with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and neighbouring countries.

 

Mr Lee welcomed enterprises from Laos and other ASEAN countries to make use of Hong Kong's leading professional services and favourable business environment to explore opportunities, and jointly promote regional co-operation and economic prosperity. He also thanked Laos for its support of Hong Kong's accession to the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership.

 

Afterwards, Mr Lee met the Minister of Trade & Integration of Kazakhstan Arman Shakkaliyev. He said today's meeting followed up on the solid outcomes achieved during his earlier visit to Kazakhstan, further advancing the "hub-to-hub" co-operation model.

 

Mr Lee also noted that, with the launch of direct flights from Hong Kong to Almaty in the first quarter of next year, and the expansion of the Economic & Trade Office network to cover Central Asia, bilateral exchanges and economic and trade co-operation will be further deepened, continuously strengthening co-operation across various sectors and jointly seizing the opportunities presented by the Belt & Road Initiative.

 

Mr Lee then met the Minister of State for Foreign Trade Affairs of Qatar Ahmed bin Mohammed Al-Sayed. He said that as the global economic gravity continues to shift eastwards, Hong Kong will continue to firmly support free trade and multilateralism, and continue to expand its global trade network, including providing safe, free and diverse investment opportunities with no capital controls for investors from the Middle East.

 

He also mentioned that Hong Kong can provide financing and professional services support for the Qatar National Vision 2030 and its economic diversification efforts, promoting broader and deeper co-operation between the two sides in finance, investment, trade, and innovation and technology.

 

Secretary for Justice Paul Lam, Deputy Financial Secretary Michael Wong, Deputy Secretary for Justice Cheung Kwok-kwan, Secretary for Commerce & Economic Development Algernon Yau, Secretary for Education Choi Yuk-lin, Secretary for Innovation, Technology & Industry Prof Sun Dong, Secretary for Transport & Logistics Mable Chan, Secretary for Culture, Sports & Tourism Rosanna Law and the Director of the Chief Executive's Office Carol Yip also attended the respective meetings.

title: CE speaks at Belt-Road Summit
body:
The 11th Belt & Road Summit is being held over two consecutive days from today at the Convention & Exhibition Centre, with Chief Executive John Lee speaking at the opening session.

 

Speaking at the opening session, Mr Lee reiterated that under “one country, two systems”, Hong Kong enjoys the strong support of China, while maintaining far-reaching international connectivity.

 

“With the world struggling with unprecedented change and geopolitical fragmentation, connectivity, co-operation and consensus are essential. That is precisely what the Belt & Road Summit offers.

 

“Hong Kong's merchandise trade with Belt & Road countries rose by nearly 17% last year, reaching about US$323 billion. Close to 1,500 companies from Belt & Road countries have established offices in Hong Kong, up about 17% from 2022. Over 100 Belt & Road companies are listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, with more in the pipeline.”

 

Vice Minister of Commerce Yan Dong said the central government will leverage Hong Kong's strengths in innovation and technology to drive co-operation in emerging fields along the Belt & Road.

 

Receiving business delegates from Hong Kong earlier this year, Prime Minister of Uzbekistan Abdulla Nigmatovich Aripov proposed digital co-operation with Hong Kong on artificial intelligence and fintech.

 

Uruguayan Vice President Carolina Cosse said China and Uruguay – the first country in Latin America to formally express its support for the Belt & Road Initiative – share core mutual interests.

 

She said Uruguay recognises Hong Kong's distinctive comparative advantages as a premier international financial, trading and shipping centre, all functioning under the constitutional framework of “one country, two systems.”

 

“We also follow with the utmost interest the development of the Greater Bay Area, of which Hong Kong is an integral part,” she added.

 

The theme of this year's summit is “Advancing High-Quality Development · Embarking on a New Journey”, and it includes sessions focused on going global, Central Asia and the Middle East.

 

Lao Deputy Prime Minister Saleumxay Kommasith said the summit has facilitated remarkable achievements across infrastructure connectivity, financial integration, digital innovation and sustainable development since its inception in 2016.

 

“As a super connector and super value-adder, Hong Kong drives multilateral co-operation, business matching and open trade, while providing the financial and professional expertise to turn dialogue into concrete achievements.”

 

The summit will witness the exchange of over 60 government-level agreements and memoranda of understanding (MOUs), as well as business MOUs and transactions with Belt & Road partners. The total value of projects and deals concluded in recent days is over US$3.1 billion.

 

More than 6,000 leaders and professionals from over 70 countries are attending the summit.

title: Going global seminar held
body:
The Task Force on Supporting Mainland Enterprises in Going Global today held a seminar to promote Hong Kong's unique advantages in going global and the opportunities offered by the Northern Metropolis (NM).

 

More than 120 representatives of central and other state-owned enterprises preparing to attend the 11th Belt & Road Summit joined the "Set Sail from Hong Kong, Harness the Power of the Northern Metropolis – Mainland Enterprises Going Global Seminar".

 

Addressing the seminar, Secretary for Commerce & Economic Development Algernon Yau said that Hong Kong, with its international business environment, world-class professional services, and top-tier talent, is the best home port for enterprises setting sail overseas.

 

Under his leadership, the task force helps enterprises go global in an orderly manner through a three-step approach of "bringing in", making preparations in Hong Kong for going global, and "reaching out".

 

He added that the NM offers enormous development potential and ample land for industrial use, which are conducive to enterprises establishing and growing their operations in Hong Kong and venturing into overseas markets with the support of Hong Kong's world-class professional services.

 

The seminar featured two thematic discussions. The first explored the industrial layout of the NM and how the opportunities arising from its modern logistics ecosystem can help internationalise the businesses of Mainland enterprises.

 

The second examined how Mainland enterprises can leverage Hong Kong's advantages to respond to the new dynamics of global commodity markets and the strains on overseas supply chains, as well as how to optimise overseas trade, commodity hedging and risk management.

title: Sci-Tech cluster maintains global lead
body:
The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government today welcomed the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) ranking of the Shenzhen-Hong Kong-Guangzhou cluster as first globally again in its Global Innovation Index 2026 top 100 innovation clusters.

 

The Government stated that the ranking reaffirmed the outstanding innovative capacity and the vibrant innovation and technology (I&T) financing ecosystem of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area.

 

WIPO evaluates world-class innovation hubs using three key metrics: international patent-filings via the Patent Cooperation Treaty, scientific publications and venture capital deals. For this year's index, the Shenzhen-Hong Kong-Guangzhou cluster recorded 2,259 Patent Cooperation Treaty applications, 4,060 scientific articles and 138 venture capital deals per 1 million inhabitants over the past five years.

 

Expediting I&T development remains a top policy priority for the current-term Government, and those efforts have started to bear fruit. The number of start-ups rose from over 1,500 in 2015 to more than 5,200 in 2025, while the city’s two I&T flagships – Hong Kong Science Park and Cyberport – have collectively nurtured around 20 unicorn enterprises.

 

Infrastructure expansion has further boosted regional integration. The Hong Kong Park of the Hetao Shenzhen-Hong Kong Science & Technology Innovation Co-operation Zone (the Loop Hong Kong Park) officially opened in December last year, with over 100 technology enterprises and institutions already signing leases.

 

By leveraging the advantages of the alliance between Hong Kong and Shenzhen, the Loop Hong Kong Park will serve as an international platform for basic scientific research, commercialisation and pilot production, driving high-quality development.

 

Additionally, the San Tin Technopole Company Limited was established in June this year to drive the development of 210 hectares of I&T land. This hub will form a vital node connecting upstream, midstream and downstream industries alongside the Loop Hong Kong Park.

 

Hong Kong also maintains a robust private equity market with assets under management close to US$250 billion, ranking second in Asia after the Chinese Mainland. 

 

Looking ahead, the Government added that Hong Kong will proactively align with the National 15th Five-Year Plan to strengthen the city’s strategic position as an international I&T centre. It emphasised that Hong Kong will further deepen collaboration with the Greater Bay Area sister cities, contributing to the country's efforts in building a modern industrial system and achieving high-level scientific and technological self-reliance and strength.

HK to deepen GBA development
body:
Hong Kong will play an active role in advancing the development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) to develop a first-class, international bay area by leveraging its strong connections with the Mainland.

 

Introducing the city’s First Five-Year Plan, Chief Executive John Lee today highlighted that the GBA serves as a strategic fulcrum of the country’s new development paradigm, demonstrating high-quality development while pioneering Chinese modernisation.

 

Hong Kong’s participation in the GBA’s development will help to elevate the region into a first-class bay area with international influence. Through the "high-end research and development advanced manufacturing-modern services" collaboration model, the city will develop an innovation and technology industry chain.

 

Under the Five-Year Plan, Hong Kong will continue to promote the “hard connectivity” of infrastructure by advancing cross-boundary railway projects and promoting the interconnectivity of computing infrastructure with other GBA cities, thereby expediting the formation of large intelligent computing clusters.

 

The city will facilitate the mutual recognition of professional qualifications in the GBA and align healthcare services and regulatory frameworks in the area. It will also enhance the mutual capital market access mechanism and facilitate the flow of personnel, materials, capital and data.

 

The plan also pledges to strengthen cooperation between Hong Kong’s higher education institutions and those in the GBA cities, and the Residential Care Services Scheme in Guangdong will be expanded.

 

The city will also create an international collaboration network. This co-operative alliance will deepen regional collaboration with the Mainland, as well as international co-operation and exchanges.

 

Guided by the Five-Year Plan, Hong Kong will actively participate in the work of international organisations, promote Chinese standards and deepen participation in high-quality Belt & Road cooperation.

 

Visit Part 4 of Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan for more details.

title: Plan aims to strengthen “four centres”
body:
Chief Executive John Lee announced today that, as part of Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan, the city will consolidate and enhance its status as an international financial, maritime and trade centre and as an international aviation hub.

 

He said the policy of “four centres and one hub” will be advanced at full steam to sharpen Hong Kong’s competitive edge and drive its economic development. 

 

International finance

Under the Five-Year Plan, Hong Kong’s open financial markets will be leveraged to attract global capital, talent, and financial enterprises, thereby strengthening the city's position as an international financial centre. 

 

Hong Kong’s role as a global offshore renminbi (RMB) business hub will be bolstered by refining the RMB Business Facility, expanding product supply in the offshore RMB market, promoting the use of RMB for pricing, settlement, and investment purposes, and supporting the wider use of RMB in cross-boundary business. 

 

Meanwhile, the city’s function as a world-leading cross-boundary wealth management centre will be reinforced through the provision of quality services for global sovereign wealth funds and family offices. Simultaneously, its role as an international risk management centre will be advanced by deepening regulatory co-operation with the Mainland and overseas markets while advancing synergy between traditional insurance and non-traditional risk management tools. 

 

The plan also pledges to enhance the competitiveness of Hong Kong’s listing regime and the operating efficiency of its securities market infrastructure, broaden the mutual access mechanism, and expedite the commercialisation, internationalisation and modernisation of the Central Moneymarkets Unit. 

 

A commodity trading ecosystem with gold as an entry point will be built by developing a clearing system, storage capacity, supply and infrastructure related to gold trading, as well as fostering innovation in commodity trading in the offshore RMB market. 

 

In addition, the Government will take forward its “Finance+” strategy to serve the real economy in areas such as innovation and technology, trade, green development, intellectual property, the maritime sector, and livelihoods.

 

Trade centre

The city’s status as international trade centre will also be strengthened, with Hong Kong continuing to uphold free trade, maintain its zero tariff approach, and support the rules-based multilateral trading system. 

 

Mr Lee said a high value-added supply chain services system will be developed, leveraging the Task Force on Supporting Mainland Enterprises in Going Global, so as to support Mainland enterprises in their international expansion. 

 

Hong Kong will also continue to pursue the comprehensive upgrading of the Closer Economic Partnership Arrangement (CEPA) between the Mainland and Hong Kong in order to achieve the expansion of access to Mainland markets. 

 

Maritime development

In the maritime sector, Hong Kong will seek to stabilise its container throughput, add value, and strengthen synergy. It will drive a “volume to value” transformation of the Hong Kong Port, advance the industry’s digitalisation, smart transition, and green transformation, and deepen co-operation with Mainland and international shipping ports. 

 

Moreover, the city will develop a high value-added maritime services ecosystem through leveraging and upgrading its existing strength in such services and reforming the ship registration regime. 

 

Aviation hub

Under the Five-Year Plan, Hong Kong will also engage deeply in the development of the national aviation network, enhance the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area’s intermodal network, and actively integrate into the country’s “one circle, six corridors, and five channels” framework. The city will continue to launch new routes, and to expand its aviation partnership network with the Belt & Road Initiative countries. 

 

At the same time, an aircraft parts processing and trading industry ecosystem will be developed, and Hong Kong will aim to achieve a Sustainable Aviation Fuel consumption ratio of 1% to 3% for flights departing from Hong Kong International Airport in 2030. The city will also be developed as the Asia-Pacific region’s hub for innovative low-altitude applications.

 

Visit Part 2 of Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan for more details.

title: Holistic view key to dev, security
body:
Chief Executive John Lee today emphasised that security is the prerequisite for development and that development reinforces security as he announced Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan.

 

Under the blueprint, public governance will be enhanced by driving a shift towards a prevention-based model to bolster the resilience of the economy and society. Various initiatives will be spearheaded to improve security and efficiency through a reform-oriented mindset, he said.

 

As part of the effort to build an efficient government, digital evolution and smart transformation of public administration will be expedited. To achieve this, technology will be leveraged to boost the efficiency of law enforcement agencies through the use of data analytics to improve surveillance to combat problems such as the abuse of public rental housing.

 

A wider adoption of the “digital-first” principle in government will be promoted in procedures and work flows, while digital identity functions and one-stop e-services powered by “IAM Smart” and the Digital Corporate Identity Platform will be expanded.

 

Meanwhile, the civil service training management system will be improved to entrench a people-oriented ethos. This will include improvements to the civil service performance appraisal system to ensure fairness in handing out rewards and punishment.

 

Additionally, under the plan, Hong Kong’s disaster prevention, mitigation and response capabilities will be strengthened. Efforts will be made to integrate the city management system, connecting city management data from different departments. By using technologies such as AI, big data and the Internet of Things for inter-departmental data sharing, real-time analysis, risk alerts, instant predictions and management synergies, the city’s resilience can be further enhanced.

 

Furthermore, under the holistic national security approach, Hong Kong’s institutions, legal system and enforcement mechanisms will be further strengthened to safeguard national security.

 

Mr Lee emphasised that the Policy Address delivered by the Chief Executive will serve as an annual work plan for implementing the Five-Year Plan. The Budget provides solid resource support for the implementation of the Five-Year Plan and the annual Policy Address.

 

The Chief Executive will report to the President of the People’s Republic of China and the Central Government on the implementation of the Five-Year Plan in the context of the annual duty visit. The implementation of the Five-Year Plan will be monitored, assessed and checked regularly, with mid-term adjustments to be made in light of actual circumstances.

 

Visit Part 6 and Part 7 of Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan for more details.

title: CE backs NM 3 university towns plan
body:
Development across the Northern Metropolis (NM) will spearhead Hong Kong’s spatial layout optimisation, anchoring Chief Executive John Lee’s First Five-Year Plan announced today with a focus on education, technology and economic expansion.

 

The blueprint expands the area of the three University Towns – San Tin, Hung Shui Kiu and Ta Kwu Ling – to over 1,000 hectares to form an area for talent development.

 

Guided by the “One Town, Five Elements” layout, the university towns integrate education, technology, industry, talent and urban development. Campus areas spanning 300 hectares will connect directly to adjacent strategic industry areas, distinctive conservation areas, recreational and cultural facilities and surrounding living communities.

 

According to the Plan, San Tin University Town is positioned to focus on medicine, life and health technology, artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, microelectronics and emerging industries. Construction will commence on the medical school of The Hong Kong University of Science & Technology alongside an integrated medical teaching and research hospital.

 

Hung Shui Kiu University Town will serve as a cultivation centre for smart manufacturing, applied post-secondary education and internationalised talent, with campus site allocations commencing in 2026 and post-secondary institutions moving in between 2027 and 2028.

 

Ta Kwu Ling University Town, meanwhile, will incorporate arts and blue-green development elements while reserving strategic space for future needs. Sites will be made available progressively from 2030 onwards to support the development of emerging industries, advanced construction industries, traditional industries and new industries.

 

To build a technology-driven industry-academia-research collaborative innovation system, the Government will expedite the development of the Hetao Shenzhen-Hong Kong Science & Technology Innovation Co-operation Zone under the vision of “one river, two banks” and “one zone, two parks”. Spatial layout, planning coordination and infrastructure connectivity between the Hong Kong and Shenzhen Parks will be aligned to facilitate the secure, efficient and convenient flow of personnel, materials, capital and data.

 

Additionally, the San Tin Technopole, the Sandy Ridge Data Facility Cluster, the Hung Shui Kiu Industry Park and modern logistics cluster, the Lau Fau Shan Digital Technology Hub, the Advanced Construction Industrial Park in Yuen Long South will form a platform for diversified industry development, and the Ta Kwu Ling New Development Area will serve as a base for emerging industries.

 

Land supply initiatives will make available about 900 hectares of “spade-ready sites” from 2026-27 to 2030-31, enabling the provision of over 70,000 housing units and 1 million square metres of economic floor space.

 

The Government will enact the Northern Metropolis Development Ordinance and its subsidiary legislation to streamline control throughout the development process and expedite bringing in industries.

 

On the transport front, infrastructure will press full steam ahead under the “Eight Vertical and Eight Horizontal Corridors” layout. Priority projects include the Northern Link Spur Line, the Hong Kong section of the Hong Kong-Shenzhen Western Rail Link, the Northern Metropolis Highway (San Tin Section), and the Tsing Lung Bridge at the Southern end of Route 11.

 

Railway accessibility will expand as Kwu Tung Station on the East Rail Line and Hung Shui Kiu Station on the Tuen Ma Line commence operation in 2027 and 2030, respectively.

 

Visit Part 3 of Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan for more details.

title: 5-Year Plan charts HK's course
body:
Chief Executive John Lee today announced the First Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) for the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, a forward-looking, strategic and directional guiding document, formulated to proactively align with national development strategies, allowing Hong Kong to better integrate into and serve overall national development.

 

While grounded in the city’s present, the blueprint lays out the medium- to long-term strategy for Hong Kong’s development. The Five-Year Plan is designed to guide directions for development, optimise resource allocation, enhance certainty over social expectations and better protect social well-being, as well as the interests of internationals investors.

 

The document ensures that Hong Kong will continue to make more substantial contributions to building a strong country and achieving national rejuvenation through the advancement of Chinese modernisation.

 

Seven principles

Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan is underpinned by seven principles, which include adhering to the “one country, two systems” principle and remaining committed to a livelihood-oriented approach to governance. At the same time, the documents stipulates that the Hong Kong SAR will uphold an executive- led system of government that will continue to embrace reform and innovation.

 

Additionally, the inaugural Five-Year Plan aims to maintain a two-pronged approach of “effective markets” and “capable government”.

 

The document also outlines a holistic approach that Hong Kong will use for development and security, as well as pragmatic and proactive planning.

 

Five objectives

The First Five-Year plan is aimed at achieving five major objectives. Among them, the document highlights that Hong Kong will achieve new breakthroughs in economic development, ensuring a more prosperous future offering new opportunities.

 

As an international city, Hong Kong will continue to leverage its advantages to boost its global competitiveness and expand its influence. Under the Five-Year Plan, the creation of the Northern Metropolis will be expedited to establish an integrated development that offers a university town, a hub for I&T and industry, and an environment suitable for living, work and travel.

 

The document also outlines a strategy to enhance social well-being through refining the Social Protection Framework.

 

The fifth objective is to make significant strides in integrating into and serving the overall national development.

 

Visit Foreword & Part 1 of Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan for more details.

title: HK to deepen GBA development
body:
Hong Kong will play an active role in advancing the development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) to develop a first-class, international bay area by leveraging its strong connections with the Mainland.

 

Introducing the city’s First Five-Year Plan, Chief Executive John Lee today highlighted that the GBA serves as a strategic fulcrum of the country’s new development paradigm, demonstrating high-quality development while pioneering Chinese modernisation.

 

Hong Kong’s participation in the GBA’s development will help to elevate the region into a first-class bay area with international influence. Through the "high-end research and development advanced manufacturing-modern services" collaboration model, the city will develop an innovation and technology industry chain.

 

Under the Five-Year Plan, Hong Kong will continue to promote the “hard connectivity” of infrastructure by advancing cross-boundary railway projects and promoting the interconnectivity of computing infrastructure with other GBA cities, thereby expediting the formation of large intelligent computing clusters.

 

The city will facilitate the mutual recognition of professional qualifications in the GBA and align healthcare services and regulatory frameworks in the area. It will also enhance the mutual capital market access mechanism and facilitate the flow of personnel, materials, capital and data.

 

The plan also pledges to strengthen cooperation between Hong Kong’s higher education institutions and those in the GBA cities, and the Residential Care Services Scheme in Guangdong will be expanded.

 

The city will also create an international collaboration network. This co-operative alliance will deepen regional collaboration with the Mainland, as well as international co-operation and exchanges.

 

Guided by the Five-Year Plan, Hong Kong will actively participate in the work of international organisations, promote Chinese standards and deepen participation in high-quality Belt & Road cooperation.

 

Visit Part 4 of Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan for more details.

title: Plan aims to strengthen “four centres”
body:
Chief Executive John Lee announced today that, as part of Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan, the city will consolidate and enhance its status as an international financial, maritime and trade centre and as an international aviation hub.

 

He said the policy of “four centres and one hub” will be advanced at full steam to sharpen Hong Kong’s competitive edge and drive its economic development. 

 

International finance

Under the Five-Year Plan, Hong Kong’s open financial markets will be leveraged to attract global capital, talent, and financial enterprises, thereby strengthening the city's position as an international financial centre. 

 

Hong Kong’s role as a global offshore renminbi (RMB) business hub will be bolstered by refining the RMB Business Facility, expanding product supply in the offshore RMB market, promoting the use of RMB for pricing, settlement, and investment purposes, and supporting the wider use of RMB in cross-boundary business. 

 

Meanwhile, the city’s function as a world-leading cross-boundary wealth management centre will be reinforced through the provision of quality services for global sovereign wealth funds and family offices. Simultaneously, its role as an international risk management centre will be advanced by deepening regulatory co-operation with the Mainland and overseas markets while advancing synergy between traditional insurance and non-traditional risk management tools. 

 

The plan also pledges to enhance the competitiveness of Hong Kong’s listing regime and the operating efficiency of its securities market infrastructure, broaden the mutual access mechanism, and expedite the commercialisation, internationalisation and modernisation of the Central Moneymarkets Unit. 

 

A commodity trading ecosystem with gold as an entry point will be built by developing a clearing system, storage capacity, supply and infrastructure related to gold trading, as well as fostering innovation in commodity trading in the offshore RMB market. 

 

In addition, the Government will take forward its “Finance+” strategy to serve the real economy in areas such as innovation and technology, trade, green development, intellectual property, the maritime sector, and livelihoods.

 

Trade centre

The city’s status as international trade centre will also be strengthened, with Hong Kong continuing to uphold free trade, maintain its zero tariff approach, and support the rules-based multilateral trading system. 

 

Mr Lee said a high value-added supply chain services system will be developed, leveraging the Task Force on Supporting Mainland Enterprises in Going Global, so as to support Mainland enterprises in their international expansion. 

 

Hong Kong will also continue to pursue the comprehensive upgrading of the Closer Economic Partnership Arrangement (CEPA) between the Mainland and Hong Kong in order to achieve the expansion of access to Mainland markets. 

 

Maritime development

In the maritime sector, Hong Kong will seek to stabilise its container throughput, add value, and strengthen synergy. It will drive a “volume to value” transformation of the Hong Kong Port, advance the industry’s digitalisation, smart transition, and green transformation, and deepen co-operation with Mainland and international shipping ports. 

 

Moreover, the city will develop a high value-added maritime services ecosystem through leveraging and upgrading its existing strength in such services and reforming the ship registration regime. 

 

Aviation hub

Under the Five-Year Plan, Hong Kong will also engage deeply in the development of the national aviation network, enhance the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area’s intermodal network, and actively integrate into the country’s “one circle, six corridors, and five channels” framework. The city will continue to launch new routes, and to expand its aviation partnership network with the Belt & Road Initiative countries. 

 

At the same time, an aircraft parts processing and trading industry ecosystem will be developed, and Hong Kong will aim to achieve a Sustainable Aviation Fuel consumption ratio of 1% to 3% for flights departing from Hong Kong International Airport in 2030. The city will also be developed as the Asia-Pacific region’s hub for innovative low-altitude applications.

 

Visit Part 2 of Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan for more details.

title: HK to leverage global strengths
body:
Hong Kong will strive to leverage its advantages as an international city and strengthen its global competitiveness under its first Five-Year Plan.

 

Announcing the plan, Chief Executive John Lee outlined that it will steer a high-end and high-value-added transformation in the city’s service sector, enable the assembly of high-end resources and talent, and drive the integrated development of industries.

 

A key area of focus will be the city’s development as an international legal and dispute resolution services centre. Under the plan, Hong Kong will leverage its unique advantages as a common law jurisdiction to develop as a hub for high-calibre legal talent, promote the closer interface of rules and mechanisms safeguarding the rule of law across the Greater Bay Area, and work with the International Organization for Mediation to further its role, thereby reinforcing Hong Kong’s status as a global mediation capital.

 

Efforts will also be made to develop Hong Kong as a regional intellectual property (IP) trading centre. Besides enhancing IP protection mechanisms in alignment with international rules, reforms to the patent system will be deepened, with a view to fostering innovation and providing more effective support for technology transformation, and for the commercialisation, and industrialisation of research and development (R&D) outcomes.

 

A thriving IP trading ecosystem will be developed, meanwhile, through exploring IP financing modes, so as to channel capital into IP-intensive areas such as innovation and technology (I&T) and the cultural and creative industries.

 

The five-year plan also covers Hong Kong’s development as an East-meets-West centre for international cultural exchange.

 

The city will develop diverse arts, culture and creative industries, as well as the ecosystem to sustain them. It will also drive wider participation in sports, develop elite sports, maintain Hong Kong’s status as a centre for major international sports events, enhance professionalism in sports in the city, and develop sports as an industry.

 

Furthermore, it will deepen the integrated development of culture, sports, and tourism, and enrich the supply of high-quality tourism products, while bolstering infrastructure and ancillary facilities. Hong Kong will develop a core demonstration zone for multi-destination tourism and facilitate visitors’ extension of their itineraries to the Greater Bay Area and other provinces and municipalities.

 

Visit Part 2 of Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan for more details.

title: CE backs NM 3 university towns plan
body:
Development across the Northern Metropolis (NM) will spearhead Hong Kong’s spatial layout optimisation, anchoring Chief Executive John Lee’s First Five-Year Plan announced today with a focus on education, technology and economic expansion.

 

The blueprint expands the area of the three University Towns – San Tin, Hung Shui Kiu and Ta Kwu Ling – to over 1,000 hectares to form an area for talent development.

 

Guided by the “One Town, Five Elements” layout, the university towns integrate education, technology, industry, talent and urban development. Campus areas spanning 300 hectares will connect directly to adjacent strategic industry areas, distinctive conservation areas, recreational and cultural facilities and surrounding living communities.

 

According to the Plan, San Tin University Town is positioned to focus on medicine, life and health technology, artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, microelectronics and emerging industries. Construction will commence on the medical school of The Hong Kong University of Science & Technology alongside an integrated medical teaching and research hospital.

 

Hung Shui Kiu University Town will serve as a cultivation centre for smart manufacturing, applied post-secondary education and internationalised talent, with campus site allocations commencing in 2026 and post-secondary institutions moving in between 2027 and 2028.

 

Ta Kwu Ling University Town, meanwhile, will incorporate arts and blue-green development elements while reserving strategic space for future needs. Sites will be made available progressively from 2030 onwards to support the development of emerging industries, advanced construction industries, traditional industries and new industries.

 

To build a technology-driven industry-academia-research collaborative innovation system, the Government will expedite the development of the Hetao Shenzhen-Hong Kong Science & Technology Innovation Co-operation Zone under the vision of “one river, two banks” and “one zone, two parks”. Spatial layout, planning coordination and infrastructure connectivity between the Hong Kong and Shenzhen Parks will be aligned to facilitate the secure, efficient and convenient flow of personnel, materials, capital and data.

 

Additionally, the San Tin Technopole, the Sandy Ridge Data Facility Cluster, the Hung Shui Kiu Industry Park and modern logistics cluster, the Lau Fau Shan Digital Technology Hub, the Advanced Construction Industrial Park in Yuen Long South will form a platform for diversified industry development, and the Ta Kwu Ling New Development Area will serve as a base for emerging industries.

 

Land supply initiatives will make available about 900 hectares of “spade-ready sites” from 2026-27 to 2030-31, enabling the provision of over 70,000 housing units and 1 million square metres of economic floor space.

 

The Government will enact the Northern Metropolis Development Ordinance and its subsidiary legislation to streamline control throughout the development process and expedite bringing in industries.

 

On the transport front, infrastructure will press full steam ahead under the “Eight Vertical and Eight Horizontal Corridors” layout. Priority projects include the Northern Link Spur Line, the Hong Kong section of the Hong Kong-Shenzhen Western Rail Link, the Northern Metropolis Highway (San Tin Section), and the Tsing Lung Bridge at the Southern end of Route 11.

 

Railway accessibility will expand as Kwu Tung Station on the East Rail Line and Hung Shui Kiu Station on the Tuen Ma Line commence operation in 2027 and 2030, respectively.

 

Visit Part 3 of Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan for more details.

title: 5-Year Plan charts HK's course
body:
Chief Executive John Lee today announced the First Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) for the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, a forward-looking, strategic and directional guiding document, formulated to proactively align with national development strategies, allowing Hong Kong to better integrate into and serve overall national development.

 

While grounded in the city’s present, the blueprint lays out the medium- to long-term strategy for Hong Kong’s development. The Five-Year Plan is designed to guide directions for development, optimise resource allocation, enhance certainty over social expectations and better protect social well-being, as well as the interests of internationals investors.

 

The document ensures that Hong Kong will continue to make more substantial contributions to building a strong country and achieving national rejuvenation through the advancement of Chinese modernisation.

 

Seven principles

Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan is underpinned by seven principles, which include adhering to the “one country, two systems” principle and remaining committed to a livelihood-oriented approach to governance. At the same time, the documents stipulates that the Hong Kong SAR will uphold an executive- led system of government that will continue to embrace reform and innovation.

 

Additionally, the inaugural Five-Year Plan aims to maintain a two-pronged approach of “effective markets” and “capable government”.

 

The document also outlines a holistic approach that Hong Kong will use for development and security, as well as pragmatic and proactive planning.

 

Five objectives

The First Five-Year plan is aimed at achieving five major objectives. Among them, the document highlights that Hong Kong will achieve new breakthroughs in economic development, ensuring a more prosperous future offering new opportunities.

 

As an international city, Hong Kong will continue to leverage its advantages to boost its global competitiveness and expand its influence. Under the Five-Year Plan, the creation of the Northern Metropolis will be expedited to establish an integrated development that offers a university town, a hub for I&T and industry, and an environment suitable for living, work and travel.

 

The document also outlines a strategy to enhance social well-being through refining the Social Protection Framework.

 

The fifth objective is to make significant strides in integrating into and serving the overall national development.

 

Visit Foreword & Part 1 of Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan for more details.
